Ant Laudes.ant: Ecce sacérdos magnus, * qui in diébus suis plácuit Deo, et invéntus est justus.
Ant Laudes.antEng: Behold an high priest, * who in his days pleased God, and was found righteous.

Ant Laudes.ant: Non est invéntus * símilis illi, qui conserváret legem Excélsi.
Ant Laudes.antEng: None was found like unto him, * to keep the Law of the Most High.

Ant Laudes.ant: Ideo jurejurándo * fecit illum Dóminus créscere in plebem suam.
Ant Laudes.antEng: Therefore the Lord assured him * by an oath that He would multiply his seed among His people.

Ant Laudes.ant: Sacerdótes Dei, * benedícite Dóminum: servi Dómini, hymnum dícite Deo. Allelúja.
Ant Laudes.antEng: O all ye Priests of God, * bless ye the Lord O all ye servants of the Lord, sing praises unto our God.

Ant Laudes.ant: Serve bone * et fidélis, intra in gáudium Dómini tui.
Ant Laudes.antEng: Good and faithful servant, * enter thou into the joy of thy Lord.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Beátus vir, * qui in lege Dómini meditátur: volúntas ejus pérmanet die ac nocte, et ómnia quæcúmque fáciet, semper prosperabúntur.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: Blessed is the man * that doth meditate in the law of the Lord; his delight is therein day and night, and whatsoever he doeth shall prosper.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Beátus iste Sanctus, * qui confísus est in Dómino, prædicávit præcéptum Dómini, constitútus est in monte sancto ejus.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: Blessed and holy is he * that putteth his trust in the Lord, that declareth the decree of the Lord, and is set upon His holy hill.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Tu es glória mea, * tu es suscéptor meus, Dómine; tu exáltans caput meum, et exaudísti me de monte sancto tuo.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: Thou, O Lord, art my glory, * Thou art a shield for me; Thou art the Lifter-up of mine head, and Thou hast heard me out of thy holy hill.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Invocántem * exaudívit Dóminus Sanctum suum; Dóminus exaudívit eum, et constítuit eum in pace.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: When His holy one called, * the Lord heard him, yea, the Lord heard him, and gave him peace.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Læténtur omnes * qui sperant in te, Dómine; quóniam tu benedixísti justo, scuto bonæ voluntátis tuæ coronásti eum.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: Let all those that put their trust in thee rejoice, O Lord, for Thou hast blessed the righteous; * Thou hast compassed him with thy favour as with a shield.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Dómine, Dóminus noster, * quam admirábile est nomen tuum in univérsa terra! quia glória et honóre coronásti Sanctum tuum, et constituísti eum super ópera mánuum tuárum.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: O Lord, our Ruler, * how excellent is thy Name in all the earth, Who hast crowned thine holy one with glory and honour, and made him to have dominion over the works of thy hands.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Dómine, * iste Sanctus habitábit in tabernáculo tuo, operátus est justítiam, requiéscet in monte sancto tuo.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: Lord, this thy Saint * shall dwell in thy tabernacle, and this that hath worked righteousness shall abide upon thy holy hill.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Vitam pétiit * a te, et tribuísti ei, Dómine: glóriam et magnum decórem imposuísti super eum; posuísti in cápite ejus corónam de lápide pretióso.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: He asked life of thee, * and Thou, O Lord, gavest it; honour and great majesty hast Thou laid upon him; Thou hast set a crown of precious stones upon his head.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Hic accípiet * benedictiónem a Dómino, et misericórdiam a Deo salutári suo: quia hæc est generátio quæréntium Dóminum.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: He shall receive * a blessing from the Lord, and mercy from the God of his salvation, for this is the generation of them that seek the Lord.

Ant Vespera.antEng: Behold an high priest, * who in his days pleased God, and was found righteous.

Ant Vespera.ant: Non est invéntus * símilis illi, qui conserváret legem Excélsi.

Ant Vespera.ant: Ideo jurejurándo * fecit illum Dóminus créscere in plebem suam.

Ant Vespera.ant: Sacerdótes Dei, * benedícite Dóminum: servi Dómini, hymnum dícite Deo. Allelúja.
Ant Vespera.antEng: O all ye Priests of God, * bless ye the Lord O all ye servants of the Lord, sing praises unto our God.

Ant Vespera.ant: Serve bone * et fidélis, intra in gáudium Dómini tui.
Ant Vespera.antEng: Good and faithful servant, * enter thou into the joy of thy Lord.

Ant 1.label: Antiphon
Ant 1.lat: Similábo eum * viro sapiénti, qui ædificávit domum suam supra petram.
Ant 1.eng: I will liken him unto a wise man, * which built his house upon a rock.

Ant 2.label: Antiphon
Ant 2.lat: Euge, serve bone * et fidélis, quia in pauca fuísti fidélis, supra multa te constítuam, intra in gáudium Dómini tui.
Ant 2.eng: Well done, thou good and faithful servant; * thou hast been faithful over a few things, I will make thee ruler over many things; enter thou into the joy of thy Lord.

Ant 3.label: Antiphon
Ant 3.lat: Hic vir despíciens mundum * et terréna, triúmphans, divítias cælo cóndidit ore, manu.
Ant 3.eng: Lo, a servant of God * who esteemed but little things earthly. And by word and work laid him up treasure in heaven.

Ant 3 summi Pontificis.label: Antiphon
Ant 3 summi Pontificis.lat: Dum esset Summus Póntifex, * terréna non métuit, sed ad cæléstia regna gloriósus migrávit.
Ant 3 summi Pontificis.eng: While he was supreme Pontiff, * he feared not earthly powers, but gloriously went his way to the heavenly kingdom.

Capitulum Laudes.label: Capitulum
Capitulum Laudes.lat: Beátus vir, qui invéntus est sine mácula, et qui post aurum non ábiit, nec sperávit in pecúnia et thesáuris. Quis est hic, et laudábimus eum? fecit enim mirabília in vita sua.
Capitulum Laudes.eng: Blessed is the rich man that is found without blemish: and that hath not gone after gold, nor put his trust in money nor in treasures. Who is he, and we will praise him? for he hath done wonderful things in his life.

Capitulum Nona.label: Capitulum
Capitulum Nona.lat: Justum dedúxit Dóminus per vias rectas, et osténdit illi regnum Dei, et dedit illi sciéntiam sanctórum: honestávit illum in labóribus, et complévit labóres illíus.
Capitulum Nona.eng: She conducted the just, when he fled from his brother's wrath, through the right ways, and showed him the kingdom of God, and gave him the knowledge of the holy things, made him honourable in his labours, and accomplished his labours.

Capitulum Sexta.label: Capitulum
Capitulum Sexta.lat: Justus cor suum trádidit ad vigilándum dilúculo ad Dóminum, qui fecit illum, et in conspéctu Altíssimi deprecábitur.
Capitulum Sexta.eng: The righteous will give his heart to resort early to the Lord that made him, and he will pray in the sight of the most High.

Hymnus Laudes.label: Hymn
Hymnus Laudes.title: Jesu, coróna célsior
Hymnus Laudes.lat:
Jesu, coróna célsior,
Et véritas sublímior,
Qui confiténti sérvulo
Reddis perénne prǽmium:

Da supplicánti cœ́tui,
Hujus rogátu, nóxii
Remissiónem críminis,
Rumpéndo nexum vínculi.

Anni revérso témpore,
Dies refúlsit lúmine,
Quo Sanctus hic de córpore
Migrávit inter sídera.

Hic vana terræ gáudia,
Et luculénta prǽdia,
Pollúta sorde députans,
Ovans tenet cæléstia.

Te, Christe, Rex piíssime,
Hic confiténdo júgiter,
Calcávit artes dǽmonum,
Sævúmque avérni príncipem.

Virtúte clarus, et fide,
Confessióne sédulus,
Jejúna membra déferens,
Dapes supérnas óbtinet.

Proínde te piíssime
Precámur omnes súpplices:
Nobis ut hujus grátia
Pœnas remíttas débitas.

Patri perénnis glória,
Natóque Patris único,
Sanctóque sit Paráclito,
Per omne semper sǽculum.
Amen.
Hymnus Laudes.eng:
Jesu, eternal truth sublime,
Through endless years the same!
Thou crown of those who through all time
Confess thy holy name:

Thy suppliant people, through the prayer
Of thy blest saint, forgive;
For his dear sake, thy wrath forbear,
And bid our spirits live.

Again returns the sacred day,
With heavenly glory bright,
Which saw him go upon his way
Into the realms of light.

All objects of our vain desire,
All earthly joys and gains,
To him were but as filthy mire;
And now with thee he reigns.

Thee, Jesu, his all-gracious Lord,
Confessing to the last,
He trod beneath him Satan's fraud,
And stood forever fast.

In holy deeds of faith and love,
In fastings and in prayers,
His days were spent; and now above
Thy heavenly feast he shares.

Then, for his sake thy wrath lay by,
And hear us while we pray;
And pardon us, O thou most high,
On this his festal day.

All glory to the Father be;
And sole Incarnate Son;
Praise, holy Paraclete, to thee;
While endless ages run.
Amen.

Hymnus Matutinum.label: Hymn
Hymnus Matutinum.title: Iste Conféssor Dómini, coléntes
Hymnus Matutinum.lat:
Iste Conféssor Dómini, coléntes
Quem pie laudant pópuli per orbem,
Hac die lætus méruit beátas
Scándere sedes.

Qui pius, prudens, húmilis, pudícus,
Sóbriam duxit sine labe vitam,
Donec humános animávit auræ
Spíritus artus.

Cujus ob præstans méritum, frequénter,
Ægra quæ passim jacuére membra,
Víribus morbi dómitis, salúti
Restituúntur.

Noster hinc illi chorus obsequéntem
Cóncinit laudem celebrésque palmas,
Ut piis ejus précibus juvémur
Omne per ævum.

Sit salus illi, decus atque virtus,
Qui, super cæli sólio corúscans,
Tótius mundi sériem gubérnat,
Trinus et unus.
Amen.
Hymnus Matutinum.eng:
This the confessor of the Lord, whose triumph
Now all the faithful celebrate, with gladness
Erst on this feast-day merited to enter
Into his glory.

Saintly and prudent, modest in behaviour,
Peaceful and sober, chaste was he, and lowly.
While that life’s vigour, coursing through his members,
Quickened his being.

Sick ones of old time, to his tomb resorting,
Sorely by ailments manifold afflicted,
Oft-times have welcomed health and strength returning,
At his petition.

Whence we in chorus gladly do him honour,
Chanting his praises with devout affection,
That in his merits we may have a portion,
Now and forever.

His be the glory, power and salvation,
Who over all things reigneth in the highest,
Earth’s mighty fabric ruling and directing,
Onely and Trinal.
Amen.

Invit.label: Antiphon
Invit.eng: The Lord, the King of Confessors, * O come, let us worship.

Lectio Prima.label: Lectio brevis
Lectio Prima.lat: Justum dedúxit Dóminus per vias rectas, et osténdit illi regnum Dei, et dedit illi sciéntiam sanctórum: honestávit illum in labóribus, et complévit labóres illíus.
Lectio Prima.eng: She conducted the just, when he fled from his brother's wrath, through the right ways, and showed him the kingdom of God, and gave him the knowledge of the holy things, made him honourable in his labours, and accomplished his labours.

Nocturn 2 Versum.label: Versicle
Nocturn 2 Versum.eng: ℣. The mouth of the righteous speaketh wisdom.
Nocturn 2 Versum.engR: ℟. And his tongue talketh judgment.

Nocturn 3 Versum.label: Versicle
Nocturn 3 Versum.lat: ℣. Lex Dei ejus in corde ipsíus.
Nocturn 3 Versum.eng: ℣. The law of his God is in his heart.
Nocturn 3 Versum.engR: ℟. None of his steps shall slide.

Oratio.label: Oratio
Oratio.lat: Adésto, Dómine, supplicatiónibus nostris, quas in beáti N. Confessóris tui sollemnitáte deférimus: ut, qui nostræ justítiæ fidúciam non habémus, ejus, qui tibi plácuit, précibus adjuvémur.
Oratio.eng: Be mindful, O Lord, of our humble prayers in this commemoration of Your Saints, so that we, who have no confidence in our own righteousness, may be helped by the merits of those who have been pleasing to You.

Responsory Breve Nona.label: Responsorium Breve
Responsory Breve Nona.lat:
℟.br. Lex Dei ejus * In corde ipsíus.
℣. Et non supplantabúntur gressus ejus.
℟. In corde ipsíus.
Glória Patri, et Fílio, et Spirítui Sancto.
℟. Lex Dei ejus * In corde ipsíus.
Responsory Breve Nona.eng:
℟.br. The law of his God * is in his heart.
℣. None of his steps shall slide.
℟. In his heart.
Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Ghost.
℟. The law of his God * is in his heart.

Responsory Breve Sexta.label: Responsorium Breve
Responsory Breve Sexta.lat:
℟.br. Os justi * Meditábitur sapiéntiam.
℣. Et lingua ejus loquétur judícium.
℟. Meditábitur sapiéntiam.
Glória Patri, et Fílio, et Spirítui Sancto.
℟. Os justi * Meditábitur sapiéntiam.

℟.br. The mouth of the righteous * speaketh wisdom.
℣. And his tongue talketh judgment.
℟. The righteous speaketh wisdom.
Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Ghost.
℟. The mouth of the righteous * speaketh wisdom.

Responsory Breve Tertia.label: Responsorium Breve
Responsory Breve Tertia.lat:
℟.br. Amávit eum Dóminus, * Et ornávit eum.
℣. Stolam glóriæ índuit eum.
℟. Et ornávit eum.
Glória Patri, et Fílio, et Spirítui Sancto.
℟. Amávit eum Dóminus, * Et ornávit eum.

℣. He clothed him with a robe of glory.
℟. And beautified him.

℟. The Lord loved him, * and beautified him.

Ant Laudes.ant: Dómine, quinque talénta * tradidísti mihi, ecce ália quinque superlucrátus sum.
Ant Laudes.antEng: Lord, Thou deliverest unto me five talents * behold, I have gained beside them five talents more.

Ant Laudes.ant: Euge, serve bone * in módico fidélis, intra in gáudium Dómini tui.
Ant Laudes.antEng: Well done, thou good servant, * thou hast been faithful in a very little, enter thou into the joy of thy Lord.

Ant Laudes.ant: Fidélis servus * et prudens, quem constítuit Dóminus super famíliam suam.
Ant Laudes.antEng: A faithful and wise servant * whom his Lord hath made ruler over His household.

Ant Laudes.ant: Beátus ille servus, * quem, cum vénerit Dóminus ejus et pulsáverit jánuam, invénerit vigilántem.
Ant Laudes.antEng: Blessed is that servant * whom his Lord, when He cometh and knocketh at the door, shall find watching.

Ant Laudes.ant: Serve bone * et fidélis, intra in gáudium Dómini tui.
Ant Laudes.antEng: Thou good and faithful servant, * enter thou into the joy of thy Lord.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Beátus vir, * qui in lege Dómini meditátur: volúntas ejus pérmanet die ac nocte, et ómnia quæcúmque fáciet, semper prosperabúntur.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: Blessed is the man * that doth meditate in the law of the Lord; his delight is therein day and night, and whatsoever he doeth shall prosper.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Beátus iste Sanctus, * qui confísus est in Dómino, prædicávit præcéptum Dómini, constitútus est in monte sancto ejus.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: Blessed and holy is he * that putteth his trust in the Lord, that declareth the decree of the Lord, and is set upon His holy hill.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Tu es glória mea, * tu es suscéptor meus, Dómine; tu exáltans caput meum, et exaudísti me de monte sancto tuo.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: Thou, O Lord, art my glory, * Thou art a shield for me; Thou art the Lifter-up of mine head, and Thou hast heard me out of thy holy hill.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Invocántem * exaudívit Dóminus Sanctum suum; Dóminus exaudívit eum, et constítuit eum in pace.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: When His holy one called, * the Lord heard him, yea, the Lord heard him, and gave him peace.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Læténtur omnes * qui sperant in te, Dómine; quóniam tu benedixísti justo, scuto bonæ voluntátis tuæ coronásti eum.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: Let all those that put their trust in thee rejoice, O Lord, for Thou hast blessed the righteous; * Thou hast compassed him with thy favour as with a shield.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Dómine, Dóminus noster, * quam admirábile est nomen tuum in univérsa terra! quia glória et honóre coronásti Sanctum tuum, et constituísti eum super ópera mánuum tuárum.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: O Lord, our Ruler, * how excellent is thy Name in all the earth, Who hast crowned thine holy one with glory and honour, and made him to have dominion over the works of thy hands.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Dómine, * iste Sanctus habitábit in tabernáculo tuo, operátus est justítiam, requiéscet in monte sancto tuo.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: Lord, this thy Saint * shall dwell in thy tabernacle, and this that hath worked righteousness shall abide upon thy holy hill.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Vitam pétiit * a te, et tribuísti ei, Dómine: glóriam et magnum decórem imposuísti super eum; posuísti in cápite ejus corónam de lápide pretióso.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: He asked life of thee, * and Thou, O Lord, gavest it; honour and great majesty hast Thou laid upon him; Thou hast set a crown of precious stones upon his head.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Hic accípiet * benedictiónem a Dómino, et misericórdiam a Deo salutári suo: quia hæc est generátio quæréntium Dóminum.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: He shall receive * a blessing from the Lord, and mercy from the God of his salvation, for this is the generation of them that seek the Lord.

Ant Vespera.ant: Dómine, quinque talénta * tradidísti mihi, ecce ália quinque superlucrátus sum.
Ant Vespera.antEng: Lord, Thou deliverest unto me five talents * behold, I have gained beside them five talents more.

Ant Vespera.ant: Serve bone * et fidélis, intra in gáudium Dómini tui.

Ant 1.label: Antiphon
Ant 1.lat: Similábo eum * viro sapiénti, qui ædificávit domum suam supra petram.
Ant 1.eng: I will liken him unto a wise man, * which built his house upon a rock.

Ant 2.label: Antiphon
Ant 2.lat: Euge, serve bone * et fidélis, quia in pauca fuísti fidélis, supra multa te constítuam, intra in gáudium Dómini tui.
Ant 2.eng: Well done, thou good and faithful servant; * thou hast been faithful over a few things, I will make thee ruler over many things; enter thou into the joy of thy Lord.

Ant 3.label: Antiphon
Ant 3.lat: Hic vir despíciens mundum * et terréna, triúmphans, divítias cælo cóndidit ore, manu.
Ant 3.eng: Lo, a servant of God * who esteemed but little things earthly. And by word and work laid him up treasure in heaven.

Ant 3 summi Pontificis.label: Antiphon
Ant 3 summi Pontificis.lat: Dum esset Summus Póntifex, * terréna non métuit, sed ad cæléstia regna gloriósus migrávit.
Ant 3 summi Pontificis.eng: While he was supreme Pontiff, * he feared not earthly powers, but gloriously went his way to the heavenly kingdom.

Capitulum Laudes.label: Capitulum
Capitulum Laudes.lat: Beátus vir, qui invéntus est sine mácula, et qui post aurum non ábiit, nec sperávit in pecúnia et thesáuris. Quis est hic, et laudábimus eum? fecit enim mirabília in vita sua.
Capitulum Laudes.eng: Blessed is the rich man that is found without blemish: and that hath not gone after gold, nor put his trust in money nor in treasures. Who is he, and we will praise him? for he hath done wonderful things in his life.

Capitulum Nona.label: Capitulum
Capitulum Nona.lat: Justum dedúxit Dóminus per vias rectas, et osténdit illi regnum Dei, et dedit illi sciéntiam sanctórum: honestávit illum in labóribus, et complévit labóres illíus.
Capitulum Nona.eng: She conducted the just, when he fled from his brother's wrath, through the right ways, and showed him the kingdom of God, and gave him the knowledge of the holy things, made him honourable in his labours, and accomplished his labours.

Capitulum Sexta.label: Capitulum
Capitulum Sexta.lat: Justus cor suum trádidit ad vigilándum dilúculo ad Dóminum, qui fecit illum, et in conspéctu Altíssimi deprecábitur.
Capitulum Sexta.eng: The righteous will give his heart to resort early to the Lord that made him, and he will pray in the sight of the most High.

Hymnus Laudes.label: Hymn
Hymnus Laudes.title: Jesu, coróna célsior
Hymnus Laudes.lat:
Jesu, coróna célsior,
Et véritas sublímior,
Qui confiténti sérvulo
Reddis perénne prǽmium:

Da supplicánti cœ́tui,
Hujus rogátu, nóxii
Remissiónem críminis,
Rumpéndo nexum vínculi.

Anni revérso témpore,
Dies refúlsit lúmine,
Quo Sanctus hic de córpore
Migrávit inter sídera.

Hic vana terræ gáudia,
Et luculénta prǽdia,
Pollúta sorde députans,
Ovans tenet cæléstia.

Te, Christe, Rex piíssime,
Hic confiténdo júgiter,
Calcávit artes dǽmonum,
Sævúmque avérni príncipem.

Virtúte clarus, et fide,
Confessióne sédulus,
Jejúna membra déferens,
Dapes supérnas óbtinet.

Proínde te piíssime
Precámur omnes súpplices:
Nobis ut hujus grátia
Pœnas remíttas débitas.

Patri perénnis glória,
Natóque Patris único,
Sanctóque sit Paráclito,
Per omne semper sǽculum.
Amen.
Hymnus Laudes.eng:
Jesu, eternal truth sublime,
Through endless years the same!
Thou crown of those who through all time
Confess thy holy name:

Thy suppliant people, through the prayer
Of thy blest saint, forgive;
For his dear sake, thy wrath forbear,
And bid our spirits live.

Again returns the sacred day,
With heavenly glory bright,
Which saw him go upon his way
Into the realms of light.

All objects of our vain desire,
All earthly joys and gains,
To him were but as filthy mire;
And now with thee he reigns.

Thee, Jesu, his all-gracious Lord,
Confessing to the last,
He trod beneath him Satan's fraud,
And stood forever fast.

In holy deeds of faith and love,
In fastings and in prayers,
His days were spent; and now above
Thy heavenly feast he shares.

Then, for his sake thy wrath lay by,
And hear us while we pray;
And pardon us, O thou most high,
On this his festal day.

All glory to the Father be;
And sole Incarnate Son;
Praise, holy Paraclete, to thee;
While endless ages run.
Amen.

Qui pius, prudens, húmilis, pudícus,
Sóbriam duxit sine labe vitam,
Donec humános animávit auræ
Spíritus artus.

Cujus ob præstans méritum, frequénter,
Ægra quæ passim jacuére membra,
Víribus morbi dómitis, salúti
Restituúntur.

Noster hinc illi chorus obsequéntem
Cóncinit laudem celebrésque palmas,
Ut piis ejus précibus juvémur
Omne per ævum.

Sit salus illi, decus atque virtus,
Qui, super cæli sólio corúscans,
Tótius mundi sériem gubérnat,
Trinus et unus.
Amen.
Hymnus1 Matutinum.eng:
This the confessor of the Lord, whose triumph
Now all the faithful celebrate, with gladness
On this feast day year by year receiveth
Merited honors.

Saintly and prudent, modest in behaviour,
Peaceful and sober, chaste was he, and lowly.
While that life’s vigour, coursing through his members,
Quickened his being.

Sick ones of old time, to his tomb resorting,
Sorely by ailments manifold afflicted,
Oft-times have welcomed health and strength returning,
At his petition.

Whence we in chorus gladly do him honour,
Chanting his praises with devout affection,
That in his merits we may have a portion,
Now and forever.

His be the glory, power and salvation,
Who over all things reigneth in the highest,
Earth’s mighty fabric ruling and directing,
Onely and Trinal.
Amen.

Oratio.label: Oratio
Oratio.lat: Deus, qui nos beáti N. Confessóris tui ánnua solemnitáte lætíficas: concéde propítius; ut cujus natalítia cólimus, étiam actiónes imitémur.
Oratio.eng: O God, Who, year by year, dost gladden us by the solemn feast-day of thy blessed confessor N., mercifully grant unto all who keep his birthday, grace to follow after the pattern of his godly conversation.

Ant Laudes.ant: Dómine, quinque talénta * tradidísti mihi, ecce ália quinque superlucrátus sum.
Ant Laudes.antEng: Lord, Thou deliverest unto me five talents * behold, I have gained beside them five talents more.

Ant Laudes.ant: Euge, serve bone * in módico fidélis, intra in gáudium Dómini tui.
Ant Laudes.antEng: Well done, thou good servant, * thou hast been faithful in a very little, enter thou into the joy of thy Lord.

Ant Laudes.ant: Fidélis servus * et prudens, quem constítuit Dóminus super famíliam suam.
Ant Laudes.antEng: A faithful and wise servant * whom his Lord hath made ruler over His household.

Ant Laudes.ant: Beátus ille servus, * quem, cum vénerit Dóminus ejus et pulsáverit jánuam, invénerit vigilántem.
Ant Laudes.antEng: Blessed is that servant * whom his Lord, when He cometh and knocketh at the door, shall find watching.

Ant Laudes.ant: Serve bone * et fidélis, intra in gáudium Dómini tui.
Ant Laudes.antEng: Thou good and faithful servant, * enter thou into the joy of thy Lord.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Beátus vir, * qui in lege Dómini meditátur: volúntas ejus pérmanet die ac nocte, et ómnia quæcúmque fáciet, semper prosperabúntur.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: Blessed is the man * that doth meditate in the law of the Lord; his delight is therein day and night, and whatsoever he doeth shall prosper.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Beátus iste Sanctus, * qui confísus est in Dómino, prædicávit præcéptum Dómini, constitútus est in monte sancto ejus.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: Blessed and holy is he * that putteth his trust in the Lord, that declareth the decree of the Lord, and is set upon His holy hill.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Tu es glória mea, * tu es suscéptor meus, Dómine; tu exáltans caput meum, et exaudísti me de monte sancto tuo.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: Thou, O Lord, art my glory, * Thou art a shield for me; Thou art the Lifter-up of mine head, and Thou hast heard me out of thy holy hill.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Invocántem * exaudívit Dóminus Sanctum suum; Dóminus exaudívit eum, et constítuit eum in pace.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: When His holy one called, * the Lord heard him, yea, the Lord heard him, and gave him peace.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Læténtur omnes * qui sperant in te, Dómine; quóniam tu benedixísti justo, scuto bonæ voluntátis tuæ coronásti eum.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: Let all those that put their trust in thee rejoice, O Lord, for Thou hast blessed the righteous; * Thou hast compassed him with thy favour as with a shield.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Dómine, Dóminus noster, * quam admirábile est nomen tuum in univérsa terra! quia glória et honóre coronásti Sanctum tuum, et constituísti eum super ópera mánuum tuárum.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: O Lord, our Ruler, * how excellent is thy Name in all the earth, Who hast crowned thine holy one with glory and honour, and made him to have dominion over the works of thy hands.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Dómine, * iste Sanctus habitábit in tabernáculo tuo, operátus est justítiam, requiéscet in monte sancto tuo.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: Lord, this thy Saint * shall dwell in thy tabernacle, and this that hath worked righteousness shall abide upon thy holy hill.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Vitam pétiit * a te, et tribuísti ei, Dómine: glóriam et magnum decórem imposuísti super eum; posuísti in cápite ejus corónam de lápide pretióso.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: He asked life of thee, * and Thou, O Lord, gavest it; honour and great majesty hast Thou laid upon him; Thou hast set a crown of precious stones upon his head.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Hic accípiet * benedictiónem a Dómino, et misericórdiam a Deo salutári suo: quia hæc est generátio quæréntium Dóminum.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: He shall receive * a blessing from the Lord, and mercy from the God of his salvation, for this is the generation of them that seek the Lord.

Ant 1.label: Antiphon
Ant 1.lat: O Doctor óptime, * Ecclésiæ sanctæ lumen, beáte N., divínæ legis amátor, deprecáre pro nobis Fílium Dei.
Ant 1.eng: O right excellent Teacher * Light of the Holy Church, N., blessed lover of the Divine Law, pray for us to the Son of God.

Ant 2.label: Antiphon
Ant 2.lat: Euge, serve bone * et fidélis, quia in pauca fuísti fidélis, supra multa te constítuam, intra in gáudium Dómini tui.
Ant 2.eng: Well done, thou good and faithful servant; * thou hast been faithful over a few things, I will make thee ruler over many things; enter thou into the joy of thy Lord.

Ant 3.label: Antiphon
Ant 3.lat: O Doctor óptime, * Ecclésiæ sanctæ lumen, beáte N., divínæ legis amátor, deprecáre pro nobis Fílium Dei.
Ant 3.eng: O right excellent Teacher * Light of the Holy Church, N., blessed lover of the Divine Law, pray for us to the Son of God.

Ant 3 summi Pontificis.label: Antiphon
Ant 3 summi Pontificis.lat: Dum esset Summus Póntifex, * terréna non métuit, sed ad cæléstia regna gloriósus migrávit.
Ant 3 summi Pontificis.eng: While he was supreme Pontiff, * he feared not earthly powers, but gloriously went his way to the heavenly kingdom.

Capitulum Laudes.label: Capitulum
Capitulum Laudes.lat: Beátus vir, qui invéntus est sine mácula, et qui post aurum non ábiit, nec sperávit in pecúnia et thesáuris. Quis est hic, et laudábimus eum? fecit enim mirabília in vita sua.
Capitulum Laudes.eng: Blessed is the rich man that is found without blemish: and that hath not gone after gold, nor put his trust in money nor in treasures. Who is he, and we will praise him? for he hath done wonderful things in his life.

Capitulum Nona.label: Capitulum
Capitulum Nona.lat: Justum dedúxit Dóminus per vias rectas, et osténdit illi regnum Dei, et dedit illi sciéntiam sanctórum: honestávit illum in labóribus, et complévit labóres illíus.
Capitulum Nona.eng: She conducted the just, when he fled from his brother's wrath, through the right ways, and showed him the kingdom of God, and gave him the knowledge of the holy things, made him honourable in his labours, and accomplished his labours.

Capitulum Sexta.label: Capitulum
Capitulum Sexta.lat: Justus cor suum trádidit ad vigilándum dilúculo ad Dóminum, qui fecit illum, et in conspéctu Altíssimi deprecábitur.
Capitulum Sexta.eng: The righteous will give his heart to resort early to the Lord that made him, and he will pray in the sight of the most High.

Hymnus Laudes.label: Hymn
Hymnus Laudes.title: Jesu, coróna célsior
Hymnus Laudes.lat:
Jesu, coróna célsior,
Et véritas sublímior,
Qui confiténti sérvulo
Reddis perénne prǽmium:

Da supplicánti cœ́tui,
Hujus rogátu, nóxii
Remissiónem críminis,
Rumpéndo nexum vínculi.

Anni revérso témpore,
Dies refúlsit lúmine,
Quo Sanctus hic de córpore
Migrávit inter sídera.

Hic vana terræ gáudia,
Et luculénta prǽdia,
Pollúta sorde députans,
Ovans tenet cæléstia.

Te, Christe, Rex piíssime,
Hic confiténdo júgiter,
Calcávit artes dǽmonum,
Sævúmque avérni príncipem.

Virtúte clarus, et fide,
Confessióne sédulus,
Jejúna membra déferens,
Dapes supérnas óbtinet.

Proínde te piíssime
Precámur omnes súpplices:
Nobis ut hujus grátia
Pœnas remíttas débitas.

Patri perénnis glória,
Natóque Patris único,
Sanctóque sit Paráclito,
Per omne semper sǽculum.
Amen.
Hymnus Laudes.eng:
Jesu, eternal truth sublime,
Through endless years the same!
Thou crown of those who through all time
Confess thy holy name:

Thy suppliant people, through the prayer
Of thy blest saint, forgive;
For his dear sake, thy wrath forbear,
And bid our spirits live.

Again returns the sacred day,
With heavenly glory bright,
Which saw him go upon his way
Into the realms of light.

All objects of our vain desire,
All earthly joys and gains,
To him were but as filthy mire;
And now with thee he reigns.

Thee, Jesu, his all-gracious Lord,
Confessing to the last,
He trod beneath him Satan's fraud,
And stood forever fast.

In holy deeds of faith and love,
In fastings and in prayers,
His days were spent; and now above
Thy heavenly feast he shares.

Then, for his sake thy wrath lay by,
And hear us while we pray;
And pardon us, O thou most high,
On this his festal day.

All glory to the Father be;
And sole Incarnate Son;
Praise, holy Paraclete, to thee;
While endless ages run.
Amen.

Ant Laudes.antEng: Lord, Thou deliverest unto me five talents * behold, I have gained beside them five talents more.

Ant Laudes.ant: Euge, serve bone * in módico fidélis, intra in gáudium Dómini tui.
Ant Laudes.antEng: Well done, thou good servant, * thou hast been faithful in a very little, enter thou into the joy of thy Lord.

Ant Laudes.antEng: A faithful and wise servant * whom his Lord hath made ruler over His household.

Ant Laudes.ant: Beátus ille servus, * quem, cum vénerit Dóminus ejus et pulsáverit jánuam, invénerit vigilántem.
Ant Laudes.antEng: Blessed is that servant * whom his Lord, when He cometh and knocketh at the door, shall find watching.

Ant Laudes.ant: Serve bone * et fidélis, intra in gáudium Dómini tui.
Ant Laudes.antEng: Thou good and faithful servant, * enter thou into the joy of thy Lord.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Beátus vir, * qui in lege Dómini meditátur: volúntas ejus pérmanet die ac nocte, et ómnia quæcúmque fáciet, semper prosperabúntur.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: Blessed is the man * that doth meditate in the law of the Lord; his delight is therein day and night, and whatsoever he doeth shall prosper.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Beátus iste Sanctus, * qui confísus est in Dómino, prædicávit præcéptum Dómini, constitútus est in monte sancto ejus.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: Blessed and holy is he * that putteth his trust in the Lord, that declareth the decree of the Lord, and is set upon His holy hill.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Tu es glória mea, * tu es suscéptor meus, Dómine; tu exáltans caput meum, et exaudísti me de monte sancto tuo.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: Thou, O Lord, art my glory, * Thou art a shield for me; Thou art the Lifter-up of mine head, and Thou hast heard me out of thy holy hill.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Invocántem * exaudívit Dóminus Sanctum suum; Dóminus exaudívit eum, et constítuit eum in pace.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: When His holy one called, * the Lord heard him, yea, the Lord heard him, and gave him peace.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Læténtur omnes * qui sperant in te, Dómine; quóniam tu benedixísti justo, scuto bonæ voluntátis tuæ coronásti eum.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: Let all those that put their trust in thee rejoice, O Lord, for Thou hast blessed the righteous; * Thou hast compassed him with thy favour as with a shield.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Dómine, Dóminus noster, * quam admirábile est nomen tuum in univérsa terra! quia glória et honóre coronásti Sanctum tuum, et constituísti eum super ópera mánuum tuárum.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: O Lord, our Ruler, * how excellent is thy Name in all the earth, Who hast crowned thine holy one with glory and honour, and made him to have dominion over the works of thy hands.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Dómine, * iste Sanctus habitábit in tabernáculo tuo, operátus est justítiam, requiéscet in monte sancto tuo.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: Lord, this thy Saint * shall dwell in thy tabernacle, and this that hath worked righteousness shall abide upon thy holy hill.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Vitam pétiit * a te, et tribuísti ei, Dómine: glóriam et magnum decórem imposuísti super eum; posuísti in cápite ejus corónam de lápide pretióso.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: He asked life of thee, * and Thou, O Lord, gavest it; honour and great majesty hast Thou laid upon him; Thou hast set a crown of precious stones upon his head.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Hic accípiet * benedictiónem a Dómino, et misericórdiam a Deo salutári suo: quia hæc est generátio quæréntium Dóminum.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: He shall receive * a blessing from the Lord, and mercy from the God of his salvation, for this is the generation of them that seek the Lord.

Capitulum Laudes.label: Capitulum
Capitulum Laudes.lat: Beátus vir, qui invéntus est sine mácula, et qui post aurum non ábiit, nec sperávit in pecúnia et thesáuris. Quis est hic, et laudábimus eum? fecit enim mirabília in vita sua.
Capitulum Laudes.eng: Blessed is the rich man that is found without blemish: and that hath not gone after gold, nor put his trust in money nor in treasures. Who is he, and we will praise him? for he hath done wonderful things in his life.

Hymnus Laudes.label: Hymn
Hymnus Laudes.title: Jesu, coróna célsior
Hymnus Laudes.lat:
Jesu, coróna célsior,
Et véritas sublímior,
Qui confiténti sérvulo
Reddis perénne prǽmium:

Da supplicánti cœ́tui,
Hujus rogátu, nóxii
Remissiónem críminis,
Rumpéndo nexum vínculi.

Anni revérso témpore,
Dies refúlsit lúmine,
Quo Sanctus hic de córpore
Migrávit inter sídera.

Hic vana terræ gáudia,
Et luculénta prǽdia,
Pollúta sorde députans,
Ovans tenet cæléstia.

Te, Christe, Rex piíssime,
Hic confiténdo júgiter,
Calcávit artes dǽmonum,
Sævúmque avérni príncipem.

Virtúte clarus, et fide,
Confessióne sédulus,
Jejúna membra déferens,
Dapes supérnas óbtinet.

Proínde te piíssime
Precámur omnes súpplices:
Nobis ut hujus grátia
Pœnas remíttas débitas.

Patri perénnis glória,
Natóque Patris único,
Sanctóque sit Paráclito,
Per omne semper sǽculum.
Amen.
Hymnus Laudes.eng:
Jesu, eternal truth sublime,
Through endless years the same!
Thou crown of those who through all time
Confess thy holy name:

Thy suppliant people, through the prayer
Of thy blest saint, forgive;
For his dear sake, thy wrath forbear,
And bid our spirits live.

Again returns the sacred day,
With heavenly glory bright,
Which saw him go upon his way
Into the realms of light.

All objects of our vain desire,
All earthly joys and gains,
To him were but as filthy mire;
And now with thee he reigns.

Thee, Jesu, his all-gracious Lord,
Confessing to the last,
He trod beneath him Satan's fraud,
And stood forever fast.

In holy deeds of faith and love,
In fastings and in prayers,
His days were spent; and now above
Thy heavenly feast he shares.

Then, for his sake thy wrath lay by,
And hear us while we pray;
And pardon us, O thou most high,
On this his festal day.

All glory to the Father be;
And sole Incarnate Son;
Praise, holy Paraclete, to thee;
While endless ages run.
Amen.

Hymnus Matutinum.label: Hymn
Hymnus Matutinum.title: Iste Conféssor Dómini, coléntes
Hymnus Matutinum.lat:
Iste Conféssor Dómini, coléntes
Quem pie laudant pópuli per orbem,
Hac die lætus méruit beátas
Scándere sedes.

Qui pius, prudens, húmilis, pudícus,
Sóbriam duxit sine labe vitam,
Donec humános animávit auræ
Spíritus artus.

Cujus ob præstans méritum, frequénter,
Ægra quæ passim jacuére membra,
Víribus morbi dómitis, salúti
Restituúntur.

Noster hinc illi chorus obsequéntem
Cóncinit laudem celebrésque palmas,
Ut piis ejus précibus juvémur
Omne per ævum.

Sit salus illi, decus atque virtus,
Qui, super cæli sólio corúscans,
Tótius mundi sériem gubérnat,
Trinus et unus.
Amen.
Hymnus Matutinum.eng:
This the confessor of the Lord, whose triumph
Now all the faithful celebrate, with gladness
Erst on this feast-day merited to enter
Into his glory.

Saintly and prudent, modest in behaviour,
Peaceful and sober, chaste was he, and lowly.
While that life’s vigour, coursing through his members,
Quickened his being.

Sick ones of old time, to his tomb resorting,
Sorely by ailments manifold afflicted,
Oft-times have welcomed health and strength returning,
At his petition.

Whence we in chorus gladly do him honour,
Chanting his praises with devout affection,
That in his merits we may have a portion,
Now and forever.

His be the glory, power and salvation,
Who over all things reigneth in the highest,
Earth’s mighty fabric ruling and directing,
Onely and Trinal.
Amen.

Ant 1.label: Antiphon

Ant 2.eng: Well done, thou good and faithful servant; * thou hast been faithful over a few things, I will make thee ruler over many things; enter thou into the joy of thy Lord.

Capitulum Laudes.label: Capitulum
Capitulum Laudes.lat: Beátus vir, qui invéntus est sine mácula, et qui post aurum non ábiit, nec sperávit in pecúnia et thesáuris. Quis est hic, et laudábimus eum? fecit enim mirabília in vita sua.
Capitulum Laudes.eng: Blessed is the rich man that is found without blemish: and that hath not gone after gold, nor put his trust in money nor in treasures. Who is he, and we will praise him? for he hath done wonderful things in his life.

Capitulum Nona.label: Capitulum
Capitulum Nona.lat: Justum dedúxit Dóminus per vias rectas, et osténdit illi regnum Dei, et dedit illi sciéntiam sanctórum: honestávit illum in labóribus, et complévit labóres illíus.
Capitulum Nona.eng: She conducted the just, when he fled from his brother's wrath, through the right ways, and showed him the kingdom of God, and gave him the knowledge of the holy things, made him honourable in his labours, and accomplished his labours.

Capitulum Sexta.label: Capitulum
Capitulum Sexta.lat: Justus cor suum trádidit ad vigilándum dilúculo ad Dóminum, qui fecit illum, et in conspéctu Altíssimi deprecábitur.
Capitulum Sexta.eng: The righteous will give his heart to resort early to the Lord that made him, and he will pray in the sight of the most High.

Hymnus Laudes.label: Hymn
Hymnus Laudes.title: Jesu, coróna célsior
Hymnus Laudes.lat:
Jesu, coróna célsior,
Et véritas sublímior,
Qui confiténti sérvulo
Reddis perénne prǽmium:

Da supplicánti cœ́tui,
Hujus rogátu, nóxii
Remissiónem críminis,
Rumpéndo nexum vínculi.

Anni revérso témpore,
Dies refúlsit lúmine,
Quo Sanctus hic de córpore
Migrávit inter sídera.

Hic vana terræ gáudia,
Et luculénta prǽdia,
Pollúta sorde députans,
Ovans tenet cæléstia.

Te, Christe, Rex piíssime,
Hic confiténdo júgiter,
Calcávit artes dǽmonum,
Sævúmque avérni príncipem.

Virtúte clarus, et fide,
Confessióne sédulus,
Jejúna membra déferens,
Dapes supérnas óbtinet.

Proínde te piíssime
Precámur omnes súpplices:
Nobis ut hujus grátia
Pœnas remíttas débitas.

Patri perénnis glória,
Natóque Patris único,
Sanctóque sit Paráclito,
Per omne semper sǽculum.
Amen.
Hymnus Laudes.eng:
Jesu, eternal truth sublime,
Through endless years the same!
Thou crown of those who through all time
Confess thy holy name:

Thy suppliant people, through the prayer
Of thy blest saint, forgive;
For his dear sake, thy wrath forbear,
And bid our spirits live.

Again returns the sacred day,
With heavenly glory bright,
Which saw him go upon his way
Into the realms of light.

All objects of our vain desire,
All earthly joys and gains,
To him were but as filthy mire;
And now with thee he reigns.

Thee, Jesu, his all-gracious Lord,
Confessing to the last,
He trod beneath him Satan's fraud,
And stood forever fast.

In holy deeds of faith and love,
In fastings and in prayers,
His days were spent; and now above
Thy heavenly feast he shares.

Then, for his sake thy wrath lay by,
And hear us while we pray;
And pardon us, O thou most high,
On this his festal day.

All glory to the Father be;
And sole Incarnate Son;
Praise, holy Paraclete, to thee;
While endless ages run.
Amen.

Hymnus Matutinum.label: Hymn
Hymnus Matutinum.title: Iste Conféssor Dómini, coléntes
Hymnus Matutinum.lat:
Iste Conféssor Dómini, coléntes
Quem pie laudant pópuli per orbem,
Hac die lætus méruit beátas
Scándere sedes.

Qui pius, prudens, húmilis, pudícus,
Sóbriam duxit sine labe vitam,
Donec humános animávit auræ
Spíritus artus.

Cujus ob præstans méritum, frequénter,
Ægra quæ passim jacuére membra,
Víribus morbi dómitis, salúti
Restituúntur.

Noster hinc illi chorus obsequéntem
Cóncinit laudem celebrésque palmas,
Ut piis ejus précibus juvémur
Omne per ævum.

Sit salus illi, decus atque virtus,
Qui, super cæli sólio corúscans,
Tótius mundi sériem gubérnat,
Trinus et unus.
Amen.
Hymnus Matutinum.eng:
This the confessor of the Lord, whose triumph
Now all the faithful celebrate, with gladness
Erst on this feast-day merited to enter
Into his glory.

Saintly and prudent, modest in behaviour,
Peaceful and sober, chaste was he, and lowly.
While that life’s vigour, coursing through his members,
Quickened his being.

Sick ones of old time, to his tomb resorting,
Sorely by ailments manifold afflicted,
Oft-times have welcomed health and strength returning,
At his petition.

Whence we in chorus gladly do him honour,
Chanting his praises with devout affection,
That in his merits we may have a portion,
Now and forever.

His be the glory, power and salvation,
Who over all things reigneth in the highest,
Earth’s mighty fabric ruling and directing,
Onely and Trinal.
Amen.

Lectio Prima.eng: She conducted the just, when he fled from his brother's wrath, through the right ways, and showed him the kingdom of God, and gave him the knowledge of the holy things, made him honourable in his labours, and accomplished his labours.

Nocturn 3 Versum.engR: ℟. None of his steps shall slide.

Oratio.label: Oratio
Oratio.lat: Adésto, Dómine, supplicatiónibus nostris, quas in beatórum N. et N. Confessórum tuórum sollemnitáte deférimus: ut, qui nostræ justítiæ fidúciam non habémus, eórum, qui tibi placuérunt, précibus adjuvémur.
Oratio.eng: Be mindful, O Lord, of our humble prayers in this commemoration of Your Saints, so that we, who have no confidence in our own righteousness, may be helped by the merits of those who have been pleasing to You.

Ant Matutinum.antEng: He asked life of thee, * and Thou, O Lord, gavest it; honour and great majesty hast Thou laid upon him; Thou hast set a crown of precious stones upon his head.

Ant 1.label: Antiphon
Ant 1.lat: Similábo eum * viro sapiénti, qui ædificávit domum suam supra petram.
Ant 1.eng: I will liken him unto a wise man, * which built his house upon a rock.

Ant 2.label: Antiphon
Ant 2.lat: Euge, serve bone * et fidélis, quia in pauca fuísti fidélis, supra multa te constítuam, intra in gáudium Dómini tui.
Ant 2.eng: Well done, thou good and faithful servant; * thou hast been faithful over a few things, I will make thee ruler over many things; enter thou into the joy of thy Lord.

Ant 3.label: Antiphon
Ant 3.lat: Hic vir despíciens mundum * et terréna, triúmphans, divítias cælo cóndidit ore, manu.
Ant 3.eng: Lo, a servant of God * who esteemed but little things earthly. And by word and work laid him up treasure in heaven.

Ant 3 summi Pontificis.label: Antiphon
Ant 3 summi Pontificis.lat: Dum esset Summus Póntifex, * terréna non métuit, sed ad cæléstia regna gloriósus migrávit.
Ant 3 summi Pontificis.eng: While he was supreme Pontiff, * he feared not earthly powers, but gloriously went his way to the heavenly kingdom.

Capitulum Laudes.label: Capitulum
Capitulum Laudes.lat: Beátus vir, qui invéntus est sine mácula, et qui post aurum non ábiit, nec sperávit in pecúnia et thesáuris. Quis est hic, et laudábimus eum? fecit enim mirabília in vita sua.
Capitulum Laudes.eng: Blessed is the rich man that is found without blemish: and that hath not gone after gold, nor put his trust in money nor in treasures. Who is he, and we will praise him? for he hath done wonderful things in his life.

Capitulum Nona.label: Capitulum
Capitulum Nona.lat: Justum dedúxit Dóminus per vias rectas, et osténdit illi regnum Dei, et dedit illi sciéntiam sanctórum: honestávit illum in labóribus, et complévit labóres illíus.
Capitulum Nona.eng: She conducted the just, when he fled from his brother's wrath, through the right ways, and showed him the kingdom of God, and gave him the knowledge of the holy things, made him honourable in his labours, and accomplished his labours.

Capitulum Sexta.label: Capitulum
Capitulum Sexta.lat: Justus cor suum trádidit ad vigilándum dilúculo ad Dóminum, qui fecit illum, et in conspéctu Altíssimi deprecábitur.
Capitulum Sexta.eng: The righteous will give his heart to resort early to the Lord that made him, and he will pray in the sight of the most High.

Hymnus Laudes.label: Hymn
Hymnus Laudes.title: Jesu, coróna célsior
Hymnus Laudes.lat:
Jesu, coróna célsior,
Et véritas sublímior,
Qui confiténti sérvulo
Reddis perénne prǽmium:

Da supplicánti cœ́tui,
Hujus rogátu, nóxii
Remissiónem críminis,
Rumpéndo nexum vínculi.

Anni revérso témpore,
Dies refúlsit lúmine,
Quo Sanctus hic de córpore
Migrávit inter sídera.

Hic vana terræ gáudia,
Et luculénta prǽdia,
Pollúta sorde députans,
Ovans tenet cæléstia.

Te, Christe, Rex piíssime,
Hic confiténdo júgiter,
Calcávit artes dǽmonum,
Sævúmque avérni príncipem.

Virtúte clarus, et fide,
Confessióne sédulus,
Jejúna membra déferens,
Dapes supérnas óbtinet.

Proínde te piíssime
Precámur omnes súpplices:
Nobis ut hujus grátia
Pœnas remíttas débitas.

Patri perénnis glória,
Natóque Patris único,
Sanctóque sit Paráclito,
Per omne semper sǽculum.
Amen.
Hymnus Laudes.eng:
Jesu, eternal truth sublime,
Through endless years the same!
Thou crown of those who through all time
Confess thy holy name:

Thy suppliant people, through the prayer
Of thy blest saint, forgive;
For his dear sake, thy wrath forbear,
And bid our spirits live.

Again returns the sacred day,
With heavenly glory bright,
Which saw him go upon his way
Into the realms of light.

All objects of our vain desire,
All earthly joys and gains,
To him were but as filthy mire;
And now with thee he reigns.

Thee, Jesu, his all-gracious Lord,
Confessing to the last,
He trod beneath him Satan's fraud,
And stood forever fast.

In holy deeds of faith and love,
In fastings and in prayers,
His days were spent; and now above
Thy heavenly feast he shares.

Then, for his sake thy wrath lay by,
And hear us while we pray;
And pardon us, O thou most high,
On this his festal day.

All glory to the Father be;
And sole Incarnate Son;
Praise, holy Paraclete, to thee;
While endless ages run.
Amen.

Hymnus Matutinum.label: Hymn
Hymnus Matutinum.title: Iste Conféssor Dómini, coléntes
Hymnus Matutinum.lat:
Iste Conféssor Dómini, coléntes
Quem pie laudant pópuli per orbem,
Hac die lætus méruit beátas
Scándere sedes.

Qui pius, prudens, húmilis, pudícus,
Sóbriam duxit sine labe vitam,
Donec humános animávit auræ
Spíritus artus.

Cujus ob præstans méritum, frequénter,
Ægra quæ passim jacuére membra,
Víribus morbi dómitis, salúti
Restituúntur.

Noster hinc illi chorus obsequéntem
Cóncinit laudem celebrésque palmas,
Ut piis ejus précibus juvémur
Omne per ævum.

Sit salus illi, decus atque virtus,
Qui, super cæli sólio corúscans,
Tótius mundi sériem gubérnat,
Trinus et unus.
Amen.
Hymnus Matutinum.eng:
This the confessor of the Lord, whose triumph
Now all the faithful celebrate, with gladness
Erst on this feast-day merited to enter
Into his glory.

Saintly and prudent, modest in behaviour,
Peaceful and sober, chaste was he, and lowly.
While that life’s vigour, coursing through his members,
Quickened his being.

Sick ones of old time, to his tomb resorting,
Sorely by ailments manifold afflicted,
Oft-times have welcomed health and strength returning,
At his petition.

Whence we in chorus gladly do him honour,
Chanting his praises with devout affection,
That in his merits we may have a portion,
Now and forever.

His be the glory, power and salvation,
Who over all things reigneth in the highest,
Earth’s mighty fabric ruling and directing,
Onely and Trinal.
Amen.

Invit.label: Antiphon
Invit.eng: The Lord, the King of Confessors, * O come, let us worship.

Lectio Prima.label: Lectio brevis
Lectio Prima.lat: Justum dedúxit Dóminus per vias rectas, et osténdit illi regnum Dei, et dedit illi sciéntiam sanctórum: honestávit illum in labóribus, et complévit labóres illíus.
Lectio Prima.eng: She conducted the just, when he fled from his brother's wrath, through the right ways, and showed him the kingdom of God, and gave him the knowledge of the holy things, made him honourable in his labours, and accomplished his labours.

Nocturn 2 Versum.label: Versicle
Nocturn 2 Versum.eng: ℣. The mouth of the righteous speaketh wisdom.
Nocturn 2 Versum.engR: ℟. And his tongue talketh judgment.

Nocturn 3 Versum.label: Versicle
Nocturn 3 Versum.lat: ℣. Lex Dei ejus in corde ipsíus.
Nocturn 3 Versum.eng: ℣. The law of his God is in his heart.
Nocturn 3 Versum.engR: ℟. None of his steps shall slide.

Oratio.label: Oratio
Oratio.lat: Deus, qui nos beatórum N. et N. Confessórum tuórum ánnua solemnitáte lætíficas: concéde propítius; ut quórum natalítiæ cólimus, étiam actiónes imitémur.
Oratio.eng: Deus, qui nos beatórum N. et N. Confessórum tuórum ánnua solemnitáte lætíficas: concéde propítius; ut quórum natalítiæ cólimus, étiam actiónes imitémur.

℟.br. Lex Dei ejus * In corde ipsíus.

℟. In corde ipsíus.
Glória Patri, et Fílio, et Spirítui Sancto.
℟. Lex Dei ejus * In corde ipsíus.

℣. None of his steps shall slide.
℟. In his heart.
Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Ghost.
℟. The law of his God * is in his heart.

℟.br. Os justi * Meditábitur sapiéntiam.
℣. Et lingua ejus loquétur judícium.
℟. Meditábitur sapiéntiam.
Glória Patri, et Fílio, et Spirítui Sancto.
℟. Os justi * Meditábitur sapiéntiam.

℟. The mouth of the righteous * speaketh wisdom.

℟. Amávit eum Dóminus, * Et ornávit eum.

Ant Matutinum.antEng: Blessed is the man * that doth meditate in the law of the Lord; his delight is therein day and night, and whatsoever he doeth shall prosper.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Beátus iste Sanctus, * qui confísus est in Dómino, prædicávit præcéptum Dómini, constitútus est in monte sancto ejus.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: Blessed and holy is he * that putteth his trust in the Lord, that declareth the decree of the Lord, and is set upon His holy hill.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Tu es glória mea, * tu es suscéptor meus, Dómine; tu exáltans caput meum, et exaudísti me de monte sancto tuo.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: Thou, O Lord, art my glory, * Thou art a shield for me; Thou art the Lifter-up of mine head, and Thou hast heard me out of thy holy hill.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Invocántem * exaudívit Dóminus Sanctum suum; Dóminus exaudívit eum, et constítuit eum in pace.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: When His holy one called, * the Lord heard him, yea, the Lord heard him, and gave him peace.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Læténtur omnes * qui sperant in te, Dómine; quóniam tu benedixísti justo, scuto bonæ voluntátis tuæ coronásti eum.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: Let all those that put their trust in thee rejoice, O Lord, for Thou hast blessed the righteous; * Thou hast compassed him with thy favour as with a shield.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Dómine, Dóminus noster, * quam admirábile est nomen tuum in univérsa terra! quia glória et honóre coronásti Sanctum tuum, et constituísti eum super ópera mánuum tuárum.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: O Lord, our Ruler, * how excellent is thy Name in all the earth, Who hast crowned thine holy one with glory and honour, and made him to have dominion over the works of thy hands.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Dómine, * iste Sanctus habitábit in tabernáculo tuo, operátus est justítiam, requiéscet in monte sancto tuo.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: Lord, this thy Saint * shall dwell in thy tabernacle, and this that hath worked righteousness shall abide upon thy holy hill.

Ant 1.label: Antiphon
Ant 1.lat: Veni, Sponsa Christi, * áccipe corónam, quam tibi Dóminus præparávit in ætérnum.
Ant 1.eng: Come, Bride of Christ, and take the everlasting crown * which the Lord hath prepared for thee.

Ant 2.label: Antiphon
Ant 2.lat: Símile est regnum cælórum * hómini negotiatóri quærénti bonas margarítas: invénta una pretiósa, dedit ómnia sua, et comparávit eam.
Ant 2.eng: The kingdom of heaven is like unto a merchantman * seeking goodly pearls, who, when he had found one pearl of great price, went and sold all that he had, and bought it.

Ant 3.label: Antiphon
Ant 3.lat: Veni, Sponsa Christi, * áccipe corónam, quam tibi Dóminus præparávit in ætérnum.
Ant 3.eng: Come, Bride of Christ, and take the everlasting crown * which the Lord hath prepared for thee.

Capitulum Laudes.label: Capitulum
Capitulum Laudes.lat: Fratres: Qui gloriátur, in Dómino gloriétur. Non enim qui seípsum comméndat, ille probátus est; sed quem Deus comméndat.
Capitulum Laudes.eng: Brothers: But he that glorieth, let him glory in the Lord. For not he who commendeth himself, is approved, but he, whom God commendeth.

Capitulum Nona.label: Capitulum
Capitulum Nona.lat: Dómine, Deus meus, exaltásti super terram habitatiónem meam, et pro morte defluénte deprecáta sum. Invocávi Dóminum, Patrem Dómini mei, ut non derelínquat me in die tribulatiónis meæ, et in témpore superbórum sine adjutório.
Capitulum Nona.eng: O Lord, my God thou hast exalted my dwelling place upon the earth and I have prayed for death to pass away. I called upon the Lord, the father of my Lord, that he would not leave me in the day of my trouble, and in the time of the proud without help.

Capitulum Sexta.label: Capitulum
Capitulum Sexta.lat: Æmulor enim vos Dei æmulatióne. Despóndi enim vos uni viro vírginem castam exhibére Christo.
Capitulum Sexta.eng: For I am jealous of you with the jealousy of God. For I have espoused you to one husband that I may present you as a chaste virgin to Christ.

Hymnus Laudes.label: Hymn
Hymnus Laudes.title: Jesu, coróna Vírginum
Hymnus Laudes.lat:
Jesu, coróna Vírginum,
Quem Mater illa cóncipit
Quæ sola Virgo párturit,
Hæc vota clemens áccipe:

Qui pergis inter lília
Septus choréis Vírginum,
Sponsus decórus glória
Sponsísque reddens prǽmia.

Quocúmque tendis, Vírgines
Sequúntur, atque láudibus
Post te canéntes cúrsitant,
Hymnósque dulces pérsonant;

Te deprecámur súpplices,
Nostris ut addas sénsibus
Nescíre prorsus ómnia
Corruptiónis vúlnera.

Virtus, honor, laus, glória
Deo Patri cum Fílio,
Sancto simul Paráclito,
In sæculórum sǽcula.
Amen.
Hymnus Laudes.eng:
Jesu, the virgins' crown, do thou
Accept us as in prayer we bow;
Born of that Virgin, whom alone
The mother and the maid we own.

Amongst the lilies thou dost feed,
By virgin choirs accompanied;
With glory decked, the spotless brides
Whose bridal gifts thy love provides.

They, wheresoe'er thy footsteps bend,
With hymns and praises still attend:
In blessèd troops they follow thee,
With dance, and song, and melody.

We pray thee therefore to bestow
Upon our senses here below
Thy grace, that so we may endure
From taint of all corruption pure.

All laud to God the Father be,
All praise, eternal Son, to thee;
All glory as is ever meet,
To God, the holy Paraclete.
Amen.

Hymnus Matutinum.label: Hymn
Hymnus Matutinum.title: Vírginis Proles Opiféxque Matris
Hymnus Matutinum.lat:
Vírginis Proles Opiféxque Matris,
Virgo quem gessit, peperítque Virgo:
Vírginis partos cánimus decóra
Morte triúmphos.

Hæc enim palmæ dúplicis beáta
Sorte, dum gestit frágilem domáre
Córporis sexum, dómuit cruéntum
Cæde tyránnum.

Unde nec mortem, nec amíca mortis
Mille pœnárum génera expavéscens,
Sánguine effúso méruit serénum
Scándere cælum.

Hujus orátu, Deus alme, nobis
Débitas pœnas scélerum remítte;
Ut tibi puro resonémus almum
Péctore carmen.

Sit decus Patri, genitǽque Proli,
Et tibi, compar utriúsque virtus,
Spíritus semper, Deus unus, omni
Témporis ævo.
Amen.
Hymnus Matutinum.eng:
Son of a virgin, maker of thy mother,
Thou, rod and blossom from a stem unstainèd,
While we a Virgin's triumphs are rehearsing,
Hear our petition!

Lo, on thy handmaid fell a two-fold blessing,
Who, in her body vanquishing the weakness,
In that same body, grace from heaven obtaining,
Bore the world witness.

Death, nor the rending pains of death appalled her;
Bondage and torment found her undefeated:
So by the shedding of her blood attained she
Heavenly guerdon.

Fountain of mercy, hear the prayers she offers;
Purge our offences, pardon our transgressions,
So that hereafter we to thee may render
Praise with thanksgiving.

Thou, the All-Father, thou, the One-Begotten,
Thou, Holy Spirit, Three in One co-equal,
Glory be henceforth thine through all the ages,
World without ending.
Amen.

Invit.label: Antiphon
Invit.eng: The Lord, the King of Virgins, * O come, let us worship.

Lectio Prima.label: Lectio brevis
Lectio Prima.lat: Dómine, Deus meus, exaltásti super terram habitatiónem meam, et pro morte defluénte deprecáta sum. Invocávi Dóminum, Patrem Dómini mei, ut non derelínquat me in die tribulatiónis meæ, et in témpore superbórum sine adjutório.
Lectio Prima.eng: O Lord, my God thou hast exalted my dwelling place upon the earth and I have prayed for death to pass away. I called upon the Lord, the father of my Lord, that he would not leave me in the day of my trouble, and in the time of the proud without help.

Nocturn 2 Versum.label: Versicle
Nocturn 2 Versum.latR: ℟. Deus in médio ejus, non commovébitur.
Nocturn 2 Versum.eng: ℣. God shall help her with His countenance.
Nocturn 2 Versum.engR: ℟. God is in the midst of her she shall not be moved.

Nocturn 3 Versum.label: Versicle
Nocturn 3 Versum.lat: ℣. Elégit eam Deus, et præelégit eam.
Nocturn 3 Versum.latR: ℟. In tabernáculo suo habitáre facit eam.
Nocturn 3 Versum.eng: ℣. God hath chosen her, and fore-chosen her.
Nocturn 3 Versum.engR: ℟. He hath made her to dwell in His tabernacle.

Oratio.label: Oratio
Oratio.lat: Indulgéntiam nobis, quǽsumus, Dómine, beáta N. Virgo et Martyr implóret: quæ tibi grata semper éxstitit, et mérito castitátis, et tuæ professióne virtútis.
Oratio.eng: O Lord, we pray thee, that thy blessed handmaiden and witness N. in whom Thou hast ever been well pleased, because of her worthy maidenhood and her mighty showing-forth of thy power, may entreat thy pardon on our behalf.

Responsory Breve Nona.lat:

℟. Et præelégit eam.

℟. Elégit eam Deus, * Et præelégit eam.

℟. And fore-chosen her.

℟. God hath chosen her, * and fore-chosen her.

℟. Deus vultu suo.

℟. Adjuvábit eam * Deus vultu suo.

℣. God is in the midst of her, she shall not be moved.
℟. With His countenance.
Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Ghost.
℟. God shall help her * with His countenance.

Responsory Breve Tertia.label: Responsorium Breve
Responsory Breve Tertia.lat:
℟.br. Spécie tua * Et pulchritúdine tua.
℣. Inténde, próspere procéde, et regna.
℟. Et pulchritúdine tua.
Glória Patri, et Fílio, et Spirítui Sancto.
℟. Spécie tua * Et pulchritúdine tua.
Responsory Breve Tertia.eng:
℟.br. In thy comeliness * and in thy beauty.
℣. Go forward, fare prosperously, and reign.
℟. In thy beauty.
Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Ghost.
℟. In thy comeliness * and in thy beauty.

Versum 2.eng: ℣. Grace is poured into thy lips.

Ant Laudes.ant: Hæc est Virgo sápiens, * et una de número prudéntum.
Ant Laudes.antEng: This is one of the wise virgins, * one chosen out of the number of the careful.

Ant Laudes.ant: Hæc est Virgo sápiens, * quam Dóminus vigilántem invénit.
Ant Laudes.antEng: This is one of the wise virgins, * whom the Lord found watching.

Ant Laudes.ant: Hæc est quæ nescívit * torum in delícto: habébit fructum in respectióne animárum sanctárum.
Ant Laudes.antEng: This, is one which hath not known the sinful bed, * she shall have fruit in the visitation of holy souls.

Ant Laudes.ant: Veni, elécta mea, * et ponam in te thronum meum, allelúja.
Ant Laudes.antEng: Come, O my chosen one, * and I will establish My throne in thee.

Ant Laudes.ant: Ista est speciósa * inter fílias Jerúsalem.
Ant Laudes.antEng: She is beautiful * among the daughters of Jerusalem.

Ant Matutinum.ant: O quam pulchra * est casta generátio cum claritáte!
Ant Matutinum.antEng: O how lovely and glorious * is the generation of the chaste.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Ante torum * hujus Vírginis frequentáte nobis dúlcia cántica drámatis.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: Sing for us again and again before this maiden's bed * the tender idylls of the play.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Revértere, * revértere, Sunamítis; revértere, ut intueámur te.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: Return, return, O Shulammith * Return, return, that we may look upon thee.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Spécie tua * et pulchritúdine tua inténde, próspere procéde, et regna.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: In thy comeliness and thy beauty, * go forward, fare prosperously, and reign.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Adjuvábit eam * Deus vultu suo: Deus in médio ejus, non commovébitur.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: God shall help * her with His countenance: God is in the midst of her; she shall not be moved.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Aquæ multæ * non potuérunt exstínguere caritátem.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: Many waters cannot * quench love.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Nigra sum, * sed formósa, fíliæ Jerúsalem; ídeo diléxit me Rex, et introdúxit me in cubículum suum.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: I am black but comely, * O ye daughters of Jerusalem; therefore hath the King loved me, and brought me into his chamber.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Trahe me post te, * in odórem currémus unguentórum tuórum: óleum effúsum nomen tuum.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: Draw me after thee * we will run after the savour of thy good ointments; thy name is as oil poured forth.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Veni, Sponsa Christi, * áccipe corónam, quam tibi Dóminus præparávit in ætérnum.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: Come, Bride of Christ, * and take the everlasting crown which the Lord hath prepared for thee.

Ant Vespera.ant: Hæc est Virgo sápiens, * et una de número prudéntum.
Ant Vespera.antEng: This is one of the wise virgins, * one chosen out of the number of the careful.

Ant Vespera.ant: Hæc est Virgo sápiens, * quam Dóminus vigilántem invénit.
Ant Vespera.antEng: This is one of the wise virgins, * whom the Lord found watching.

Ant Vespera.ant: Hæc est quæ nescívit * torum in delícto: habébit fructum in respectióne animárum sanctárum.
Ant Vespera.antEng: This, is one which hath not known the sinful bed, * she shall have fruit in the visitation of holy souls.

Ant Vespera.ant: Veni, elécta mea, * et ponam in te thronum meum, allelúja.
Ant Vespera.antEng: Come, O my chosen one, * and I will establish My throne in thee.

Ant Vespera.ant: Ista est speciósa * inter fílias Jerúsalem.
Ant Vespera.antEng: She is beautiful * among the daughters of Jerusalem.

Ant 1.label: Antiphon
Ant 1.lat: Veni, Sponsa Christi, * áccipe corónam, quam tibi Dóminus præparávit in ætérnum.
Ant 1.eng: Come, Bride of Christ, and take the everlasting crown * which the Lord hath prepared for thee.

Ant 2.label: Antiphon
Ant 2.lat: Símile est regnum cælórum * hómini negotiatóri quærénti bonas margarítas: invénta una pretiósa, dedit ómnia sua, et comparávit eam.
Ant 2.eng: The kingdom of heaven is like unto a merchantman * seeking goodly pearls, who, when he had found one pearl of great price, went and sold all that he had, and bought it.

Ant 3.label: Antiphon
Ant 3.lat: Veni, Sponsa Christi, * áccipe corónam, quam tibi Dóminus præparávit in ætérnum.
Ant 3.eng: Come, Bride of Christ, and take the everlasting crown * which the Lord hath prepared for thee.

Capitulum Laudes.label: Capitulum
Capitulum Laudes.lat: Fratres: Qui gloriátur, in Dómino gloriétur. Non enim qui seípsum comméndat, ille probátus est; sed quem Deus comméndat.
Capitulum Laudes.eng: Brothers: But he that glorieth, let him glory in the Lord. For not he who commendeth himself, is approved, but he, whom God commendeth.

Oratio.eng: O God, Who among the other miracles of thy power have bestowed the victory of martyrdom even upon the weaker sex, graciously grant that we who commemorate the anniversary of the death of blessed N., thy Virgin and Martyr, may come to thee by the path of her example.

Hymnus Laudes.label: Hymn
Hymnus Laudes.title: Jesu, coróna Vírginum
Hymnus Laudes.lat:
Jesu, coróna Vírginum,
Quem Mater illa cóncipit
Quæ sola Virgo párturit,
Hæc vota clemens áccipe:

Qui pergis inter lília
Septus choréis Vírginum,
Sponsus decórus glória
Sponsísque reddens prǽmia.

Quocúmque tendis, Vírgines
Sequúntur, atque láudibus
Post te canéntes cúrsitant,
Hymnósque dulces pérsonant;

Te deprecámur súpplices,
Nostris ut addas sénsibus
Nescíre prorsus ómnia
Corruptiónis vúlnera.

Virtus, honor, laus, glória
Deo Patri cum Fílio,
Sancto simul Paráclito,
In sæculórum sǽcula.
Amen.
Hymnus Laudes.eng:
Jesu, the virgins' crown, do thou
Accept us as in prayer we bow;
Born of that Virgin, whom alone
The mother and the maid we own.

Amongst the lilies thou dost feed,
By virgin choirs accompanied;
With glory decked, the spotless brides
Whose bridal gifts thy love provides.

They, wheresoe'er thy footsteps bend,
With hymns and praises still attend:
In blessèd troops they follow thee,
With dance, and song, and melody.

We pray thee therefore to bestow
Upon our senses here below
Thy grace, that so we may endure
From taint of all corruption pure.

All laud to God the Father be,
All praise, eternal Son, to thee;
All glory as is ever meet,
To God, the holy Paraclete.
Amen.

Hymnus Matutinum.label: Hymn
Hymnus Matutinum.title: Vírginis Proles, Opiféxque Matris
Hymnus Matutinum.lat:
Vírginis Proles, Opiféxque Matris,
Virgo quem gessit, peperítque Virgo:
Vírginis festum cánimus beátæ,
Accipe votum.

Hujus orátu, Deus alme, nobis
Débitas pœnas scélerum remítte;
Ut tibi puro resonémus almum
Péctore carmen.

Sit decus Patri, genitǽque Proli,
Et tibi, compar utriúsque virtus,
Spíritus semper, Deus unus, omni
Témporis ævo.
Amen.
Hymnus Matutinum.eng:
Son of a virgin, maker of thy mother,
Thou, rod and blossom from a stem unstainèd,
Now while a virgin fair of fame we honour,
Hear our devotion!

Fountain of mercy, hear the prayers she offers;
Purge our offences, pardon our transgressions,
So that hereafter we to thee may render
Praise with thanksgiving.

Thou, the All-Father, thou, the One-Begotten,
Thou, Holy Spirit, Three in One co-equal,
Glory be henceforth thine through all the ages,
World without ending.
Amen.

Thou, rod and blossom from a stem unstainèd,
Now while a virgin fair of fame we honour,
Hear our devotion!

Fountain of mercy, hear the prayers she offers;
Purge our offences, pardon our transgressions,
So that hereafter we to thee may render
Praise with thanksgiving.

Thou, the All-Father, thou, the One-Begotten,
Thou, Holy Spirit, Three in One co-equal,
Glory be henceforth thine through all the ages,
World without ending.
Amen.

Hymnus Matutinum Virgo tantum.label: Hymn
Hymnus Matutinum Virgo tantum.title: Vírginis Proles, Opiféxque Matris

Vírginis Proles, Opiféxque Matris,

Vírginis festum cánimus beátæ,
Accipe votum.

Jesu, coróna Vírginum,
Quem Mater illa cóncipit
Quæ sola Virgo párturit,
Hæc vota clemens áccipe:

Qui pergis inter lília
Septus choréis Vírginum,
Sponsus decórus glória
Sponsísque reddens prǽmia.

Quocúmque tendis, Vírgines
Sequúntur, atque láudibus
Post te canéntes cúrsitant,
Hymnósque dulces pérsonant;

Te deprecámur súpplices,
Nostris ut addas sénsibus
Nescíre prorsus ómnia
Corruptiónis vúlnera.

Virtus, honor, laus, glória
Deo Patri cum Fílio,
Sancto simul Paráclito,
In sæculórum sǽcula.
Amen.
Hymnus Vespera.eng:
Jesu, the virgins' crown, do thou
Accept us as in prayer we bow;
Born of that Virgin, whom alone
The mother and the maid we own.

Amongst the lilies thou dost feed,
By virgin choirs accompanied;
With glory decked, the spotless brides
Whose bridal gifts thy love provides.

They, wheresoe'er thy footsteps bend,
With hymns and praises still attend:
In blessèd troops they follow thee,
With dance, and song, and melody.

We pray thee therefore to bestow
Upon our senses here below
Thy grace, that so we may endure
From taint of all corruption pure.

All laud to God the Father be,
All praise, eternal Son, to thee;
All glory as is ever meet,
To God, the holy Paraclete.
Amen.

Lectio Prima.label: Lectio brevis
Lectio Prima.lat: O quam pulchra est casta generátio cum claritáte! Immortális est enim memória illíus, quóniam apud Deum nota est, et apud hómines.
Lectio Prima.eng: O how beautiful is the chaste generation with glory: for the memory thereof is immortal: because it is known both with God and with men.

Ant Matutinum.antEng: Return, return, O Shulammith * Return, return, that we may look upon thee.

Capitulum Laudes.label: Capitulum
Capitulum Laudes.lat: Fratres: Qui gloriátur, in Dómino gloriétur. Non enim qui seípsum comméndat, ille probátus est; sed quem Deus comméndat.
Capitulum Laudes.eng: Brothers: But he that glorieth, let him glory in the Lord. For not he who commendeth himself, is approved, but he, whom God commendeth.

Capitulum Nona.label: Capitulum
Capitulum Nona.lat: Dómine, Deus meus, exaltásti super terram habitatiónem meam, et pro morte defluénte deprecáta sum. Invocávi Dóminum, Patrem Dómini mei, ut non derelínquat me in die tribulatiónis meæ, et in témpore superbórum sine adjutório.
Capitulum Nona.eng: O Lord, my God thou hast exalted my dwelling place upon the earth and I have prayed for death to pass away. I called upon the Lord, the father of my Lord, that he would not leave me in the day of my trouble, and in the time of the proud without help.

Capitulum Sexta.label: Capitulum
Capitulum Sexta.lat: Æmulor enim vos Dei æmulatióne. Despóndi enim vos uni viro vírginem castam exhibére Christo.
Capitulum Sexta.eng: For I am jealous of you with the jealousy of God. For I have espoused you to one husband that I may present you as a chaste virgin to Christ.

Hymnus Matutinum.label: Hymn
Hymnus Matutinum.title: Vírginis Proles Opiféxque Matris
Hymnus Matutinum.lat:
Vírginis Proles Opiféxque Matris,
Virgo quem gessit, peperítque Virgo:
Vírginis partos cánimus decóra
Morte triúmphos.

Hæc enim palmæ dúplicis beáta
Sorte, dum gestit frágilem domáre
Córporis sexum, dómuit cruéntum
Cæde tyránnum.

Unde nec mortem, nec amíca mortis
Mille pœnárum génera expavéscens,
Sánguine effúso méruit serénum
Scándere cælum.

Hujus orátu, Deus alme, nobis
Débitas pœnas scélerum remítte;
Ut tibi puro resonémus almum
Péctore carmen.

Sit decus Patri, genitǽque Proli,
Et tibi, compar utriúsque virtus,
Spíritus semper, Deus unus, omni
Témporis ævo.
Amen.
Hymnus Matutinum.eng:
Son of a virgin, maker of thy mother,
Thou, rod and blossom from a stem unstainèd,
While we a Virgin's triumphs are rehearsing,
Hear our petition!

Lo, on thy handmaid fell a two-fold blessing,
Who, in her body vanquishing the weakness,
In that same body, grace from heaven obtaining,
Bore the world witness.

Death, nor the rending pains of death appalled her;
Bondage and torment found her undefeated:
So by the shedding of her blood attained she
Heavenly guerdon.

Fountain of mercy, hear the prayers she offers;
Purge our offences, pardon our transgressions,
So that hereafter we to thee may render
Praise with thanksgiving.

Thou, the All-Father, thou, the One-Begotten,
Thou, Holy Spirit, Three in One co-equal,
Glory be henceforth thine through all the ages,
World without ending.
Amen.

Oratio.label: Oratio
Oratio.lat: Da nobis, quǽsumus, Dómine Deus noster, sanctárum Vírginum et Mártyrum tuárum N. et N. palmas incessábili devotióne venerári: ut quas digna mente non póssumus celebráre, humílibus saltem frequentémus obséquiis.
Oratio.eng: Grant unto us, we beseech thee, O Lord, our God, that we may ever call to mind, with all worship and thanksgiving, the victory of thy holy Virgins and Martyrs N. and N., and although we know that our mind cannot comprehend thee who art this day their exceeding great reward, give us always the grace humbly to worship thee.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Revértere, * revértere, Sunamítis; revértere, ut intueámur te.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: Return, return, O Shulammith * Return, return, that we may look upon thee.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Spécie tua * et pulchritúdine tua inténde, próspere procéde, et regna.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: In thy comeliness and thy beauty, * go forward, fare prosperously, and reign.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Adjuvábit eam * Deus vultu suo: Deus in médio ejus, non commovébitur.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: God shall help * her with His countenance: God is in the midst of her; she shall not be moved.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Aquæ multæ * non potuérunt exstínguere caritátem.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: Many waters cannot * quench love.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Nigra sum, * sed formósa, fíliæ Jerúsalem; ídeo diléxit me Rex, et introdúxit me in cubículum suum.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: I am black but comely, * O ye daughters of Jerusalem; therefore hath the King loved me, and brought me into his chamber.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Trahe me post te, * in odórem currémus unguentórum tuórum: óleum effúsum nomen tuum.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: Draw me after thee * we will run after the savour of thy good ointments; thy name is as oil poured forth.

Ant Matutinum.ant: Veni, Sponsa Christi, * áccipe corónam, quam tibi Dóminus præparávit in ætérnum.
Ant Matutinum.antEng: Come, Bride of Christ, * and take the everlasting crown which the Lord hath prepared for thee.

Ant Vespera.ant: Hæc est Virgo sápiens, * et una de número prudéntum.
Ant Vespera.antEng: This is one of the wise virgins, * one chosen out of the number of the careful.

Ant Vespera.ant: Hæc est Virgo sápiens, * quam Dóminus vigilántem invénit.
Ant Vespera.antEng: This is one of the wise virgins, * whom the Lord found watching.

Ant Vespera.ant: Hæc est quæ nescívit * torum in delícto: habébit fructum in respectióne animárum sanctárum.
Ant Vespera.antEng: This, is one which hath not known the sinful bed, * she shall have fruit in the visitation of holy souls.

Ant Vespera.ant: Veni, elécta mea, * et ponam in te thronum meum, allelúja.
Ant Vespera.antEng: Come, O my chosen one, * and I will establish My throne in thee.

Ant 1.label: Antiphon
Ant 1.lat: Símile est regnum cælórum * hómini negotiatóri quærénti bonas margarítas: invénta una pretiósa, dedit ómnia sua, et comparávit eam.
Ant 1.eng: The kingdom of heaven is like unto a merchantman * seeking goodly pearls, who, when he had found one pearl of great price, went and sold all that he had, and bought it.

Ant 2.label: Antiphon
Ant 2.lat: Date ei * de fructu mánuum suárum, et laudent eam in portis ópera ejus.
Ant 2.eng: Give her of the fruit of her hands, * and let her own works praise her in the gates.

Ant 3.label: Antiphon
Ant 3.lat: Manum suam * apéruit ínopi, et palmas suas exténdit ad páuperem, et panem otiósa non comédit.
Ant 3.eng: She spreadeth out her hand to the poor, * yea, she reacheth forth her hands to the needy, and eateth not the bread of idleness.

Capitulum Laudes.label: Capitulum
Capitulum Laudes.lat: Confitébor tibi, Dómine, Rex, et collaudábo te Deum Salvatórem meum. Confitébor nómini tuo: quóniam adjútor et protéctor factus es mihi, et liberásti corpus meum a perditióne.
Capitulum Laudes.eng: I will give glory to thee, O Lord, O King, and I will praise thee, O God my Saviour. I will give glory to thy name: for thou hast been a helper and protector to me, and hast preserved my body from destruction.

Capitulum Nona.label: Capitulum
Capitulum Nona.lat: Laudábit usque ad mortem ánima mea Dóminum, quóniam éruis sustinéntes te, et líberas eos de manu angústiæ, Dómine, Deus noster.
Capitulum Nona.eng: My soul shall praise the Lord even to death. How thou deliverest them that wait for thee, O Lord, and savest them out of the hands of the nations!

Capitulum Sexta.label: Capitulum
Capitulum Sexta.lat: Liberásti me secúndum multitúdinem misericórdiæ nóminis tui a rugiéntibus, præparátis ad escam, de mánibus quæréntium ánimam meam, et de multis tribulatiónibus quæ circumdedérunt me.
Capitulum Sexta.eng: And thou hast delivered me, according to the multitude of the mercy of thy name, from them that did roar, prepared to devour. Out of the hands of them that sought my life, and from the gates of afflictions, which compassed me about.

Hymnus Laudes.label: Hymn
Hymnus Laudes.title: Fortem viríli péctore
Hymnus Laudes.lat:
Fortem viríli péctore
Laudémus omnes féminam,
Quæ sanctitátis glória
Ubíque fulget ínclita.

Hæc sancto amóre sáucia,
Dum mundi amórem nóxium
Horréscit, ad cæléstia
Iter perégit árduum.

Carnem domans jejúniis,
Dulcíque mentem pábulo
Oratiónis nútriens,
Cæli potítur gáudiis.

Rex Christe, virtus fórtium,
Qui magna solus éfficis,
Hujus precátu, quǽsumus,
Audi benígnus súpplices.

Deo Patri sit glória,
Ejúsque soli Fílio,
Cum Spíritu Paráclito,
Nunc, et per omne sǽculum.
Amen.
Hymnus Laudes.eng:
High let us all our voices raise
In that heroic woman's praise
Whose name, with saintly glory bright,
Shines in the starry realms of light.

Filled with a pure celestial glow,
She spurned all love of things below;
And heedless here on earth to stay,
Climbed to the skies her toilsome way.

With fasts her body she subdued,
But filled her soul with prayer's sweet food:
In other worlds she tastes the bliss
For which she left the joys of this.

O Christ, the strength of all the strong;
To whom our holiest deeds belong!
Through her prevailing prayers on high,
In mercy hear thy people's cry!

To God the Father, with the Son,
And Holy Spirit, Three in One,
Be glory while the ages flow,
From all above, and all below.
Amen.

Hymnus Matutinum.label: Hymn
Hymnus Matutinum.title: Hujus orátu, Deus alme, nobis
Hymnus Matutinum.lat:
Hujus orátu, Deus alme, nobis
Débitas pœnas scélerum remítte;
Ut tibi puro resonémus almum
Péctore carmen.

Sit decus Patri, genitǽque Proli,
Et tibi, compar utriúsque virtus,
Spíritus semper, Deus unus, omni
Témporis ævo.
Amen.
Hymnus Matutinum.eng:
Fountain of mercy, hear the prayers she offers;
Purge our offences, pardon our transgressions,
So that hereafter we to thee may render
Praise with thanksgiving.

Thou, the All-Father, thou, the One-Begotten,
Thou, Holy Spirit, Three in One co-equal,
Glory be henceforth thine through all the ages,
World without ending.
Amen.

Oratio.eng: O God, Who, amidst the wondrous work of thy divine power, dost make even weak women to be more than conquerors in the uplifting of their testimony, mercifully grant unto all us which do keep the birthday of thy blessed witness N., grace to follow her steps toward thee.

Capitulum Laudes.eng: Who shall find a valiant woman? Far and from the uttermost coasts is the price of her. The heart of her husband trusteth in her, and he shall have no need of spoils.
